consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is Noah’s flood as divine judgment on sin paired with preservation of a righteous remnant, fixed by NT typology as prefiguring baptism and as eschatological warning of sudden final judgment; common alternatives include de-creation/re-creation and (secondarily) overwhelming trouble or enemy invasion.
book_summary: Flood means destroying waters that are peoples in motion: a nation invading or the Lord’s own host sweeping the enemy away.
consensus_core_identification: Noahic deluge = God’s judgment on wickedness + salvation of remnant (with baptismal/eschatological typology)
book_core_identification: Destroying waters = peoples in motion (invading nation or divine host)
boundary_disagreement: Consensus centers the term on the Genesis flood event and its explicit NT interpretations; the book reassigns it exclusively to prophetic military-invasion metaphors and omits Noah entirely.
material_contradiction: The book replaces the Noahic judgment-salvation complex (and its baptismal/eschatological readings) with invading armies as the core referent of “Flood.”
rationale: Minimum cores cannot be reconciled: consensus (and every listed primary) identifies the Flood as the Noah narrative and its typologies, while the book identifies it as the prophetic trope of armies-as-waters. Although “enemy invasion” appears among consensus alternatives and shares two of the book’s citations, that does not preserve the central referent; accepting the book’s entry requires discarding the settled Noahic core. Hence DIVERGENT with DIFFERENT_REFERENT, not mere boundary refinement or novelty.
strongest_objection: The entry ignores the dominant biblical and historic-Christian identification of “the Flood” with Noah’s deluge and the NT texts that explicitly interpret it.
